title: OOP & SOLID principles
relevance: High — the vocabulary and judgment bar for every LLD / machine-coding round (campus + experienced); Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Amazon, Atlassian, and most Indian product cos grill class design against these before patterns.
company_notes: Campus/new-grad LLD and machine-coding rounds almost always open with OOP pillars and applying SOLID (Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Amazon, Razorpay, Atlassian-style). Mid/experienced rounds grade why this interface or why not inherit on parking lot, Splitwise, elevator, booking, and game designs. Foundational for all LLD; explicit SOLID quizzes common early in Indian product loops and as follow-ups during machine-coding review.

phases.goal: Candidate can name the four OOP pillars and state each SOLID letter’s intent in interview terms.

must_hit.point: Four pillars: Encapsulation hides state and exposes validated operations; Abstraction shows what and hides how; Inheritance shares is-a contracts carefully; Polymorphism is one interface with many behaviors and the engine of extensible LLD.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names all four and gives a crisp one-liner for each without collapsing encapsulation into abstraction.

must_hit.point: Prefer composition/HAS-A over deep inheritance: inherit for true subtype contracts; compose for reusable behavior (Strategy, pricing engines, payment gateways).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says inherit only for real is-a; reuse behavior via HAS-A/composition with an LLD example.

must_hit.point: SRP: a class should have one reason to change, often one business actor—not merely “one method”; God classes (ParkingLot that also bills, notifies, and persists) fail LLD reviews.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties SRP to actor/axis of change and flags a multi-concern God class as a review fail.

must_hit.point: OCP: open for extension, closed for modification—add a new vehicle/fare/payment type via new class and polymorphism, not another switch branch in stable code.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes extending by new type/class rather than editing stable switch/if logic.

probes: Walk me through the four OOP pillars, then give me one sentence each for SRP and OCP in an LLD setting.

hints.1: Start with encapsulation vs abstraction, then inheritance vs polymorphism.
hints.2: SRP is about one reason to change / one actor; OCP is extend without rewriting stable policy.
hints.3: Say: hide state behind validated ops; show what not how; careful is-a; one interface many behaviors—then SRP = one actor to change, OCP = new class + polymorphism not another switch.

phases.goal: Candidate can apply LSP, ISP, and DIP correctly and spot classic hierarchy/interface coupling smells.

must_hit.point: LSP: subtypes must honor the base contract; throwing UnsupportedOperationException or weakening preconditions (Square/Rectangle, Bicycle/startEngine) is an inheritance smell → redesign the hierarchy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives a subtype that breaks the base contract and says redesign the hierarchy rather than stub/throw.

must_hit.point: ISP: don’t force clients onto fat interfaces; split by role (Parkable vs Chargeable) so implementers aren’t stubbing unused methods.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Splits a fat interface into role-specific ones so clients/implementers only see what they use.

must_hit.point: DIP: high-level policy depends on abstractions, not concretions—inject PaymentGateway, don’t new StripeClient() inside the service (also unlocks testing).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says inject an abstraction at the boundary instead of constructing a concrete client inside the service.

must_hit.point: Supporting heuristics: DRY (don’t copy domain rules); KISS/YAGNI—in a 90-min machine-coding round, a working SRP/OCP design beats a half-finished pattern zoo.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions not over-applying patterns in a timed round and keeping a working SRP/OCP core.

probes: ElectricCar implements Car but throws on turnOnEngine—what principle is broken, and how do you redesign it? Then how would ISP and DIP show up on a fat Machine with print/scan/fax?

hints.1: Ask whether every subtype can honor the parent’s promises.
hints.2: LSP → fix the abstraction; ISP → split by role; DIP → depend on injected interfaces.
hints.3: Classic LSP fail: redesign with start()/capability interfaces; segregate Printer/Scanner/Fax; DocumentService depends on a Printer abstraction injected at construction, not a concrete HpPrinter.

phases.goal: Candidate judges when to inherit, when to compose, and how far to push SOLID in a timed LLD round.

must_hit.point: Inheritance for reuse couples you to parent APIs and often violates LSP; composition + delegation reuses behavior without fake is-a (Replace Inheritance with Delegation when is-a is fake).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects inherit-everything-for-reuse and prefers composition/delegation when the is-a story is weak.

must_hit.point: Not every new feature needs a new interface—apply OCP/DIP where change is likely (payment, pricing, vehicle type); YAGNI elsewhere in a timed round.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Selectively applies interfaces where variation is expected and invokes YAGNI for the rest.

must_hit.point: Working code vs perfect SOLID: mandatory requirements plus a clean core model win; call out follow-up refactors you’d do with more time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Prioritizes a runnable happy path with a sound core, then names later SOLID cleanups.

probes: Why not inherit everything for reuse? And in a timed machine-coding round, when would you skip introducing another interface?

hints.1: Think about fake is-a and what you actually need to ship.
hints.2: Composition avoids unused inherited APIs; YAGNI limits SOLID to likely change points.
hints.3: Inherit only true subtypes; compose for shared behavior; reserve OCP/DIP for payment/pricing/vehicle-type; ship mandatory requirements first and name follow-up refactors.

phases.goal: Candidate can run pillar/SOLID drills and a short machine-coding design checklist before coding.

must_hit.point: For BankAccount: encapsulation (private balance + withdraw), abstraction (Account API), inheritance vs composition choice, polymorphism (Savings vs Current interest).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps each pillar onto BankAccount with concrete private state, API, and Savings/Current behavior.

must_hit.point: SRP smell: UserManager that authenticates, updates profile, and sends email—split into classes and state each one’s single reason to change.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Splits auth, profile, and email into separate classes with one change reason each.

must_hit.point: OCP drill: refactor PriceCalculator if (type == ...) to a PricingStrategy (or shape/area) hierarchy so a new type needs zero edits to the calculator.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Replaces type switches with strategy/polymorphism and claims the calculator stays untouched for new types.

must_hit.point: Machine-coding checklist: for a tiny system (vending machine / parking spot allocator), spend 10 minutes listing entities, IS-A vs HAS-A, and which SOLID moves you’ll use; only then code a working happy path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes a short design pass (entities, IS-A/HAS-A, SOLID moves) before coding the happy path.

probes: Take a ParkingLot-style design: where do you use composition vs inheritance, and which SOLID moves would you apply before you start coding?

hints.1: List entities and behaviors before classes.
hints.2: Mark true is-a vs has-a; put pricing/payment/vehicle variation behind abstractions.
hints.3: Entities + IS-A/HAS-A map; SRP off the God ParkingLot; OCP via strategy/polymorphism for new types; inject payment abstractions; then code the happy path.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Inherit only for true subtype contracts; prefer composition/HAS-A for reusable behavior. Inheritance couples to parent APIs and often violates LSP; composition + delegation reuses behavior without fake is-a.

tradeoffs.topic: New interface for every feature vs YAGNI
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Apply OCP/DIP where change is likely (payment, pricing, vehicle type); YAGNI elsewhere in a timed round—don’t invent interfaces you don’t need.
Mandatory requirements plus a clean core model win in machine-coding; name follow-up SOLID refactors you’d do with more time rather than shipping a half-finished pattern zoo.
SRP is one axis of change / one actor, not “small classes.” A cohesive large domain class can be fine; a small class with two stakeholders is not.

gotchas.correction: SRP means one reason to change (often one business actor). A cohesive 200-line domain class can be fine; a 50-line class with two stakeholders is not.
Inheritance couples you to parent APIs and often violates LSP; composition + delegation reuses behavior without fake is-a.

gotchas.trap: Adding a new interface for every feature.
gotchas.correction: No—apply OCP/DIP where change is likely; YAGNI elsewhere in a timed round.

gotchas.trap: ElectricCar implements Car but throws on turnOnEngine.
gotchas.correction: Classic LSP failure; redesign the abstraction (e.g. start() / capability interfaces).
Patterns are applications of SOLID (Strategy ≈ OCP+composition; DI ≈ DIP). Don’t name a pattern you didn’t need.

gotchas.trap: Chasing perfect SOLID over a working solution.
gotchas.correction: Mandatory requirements + clean core model win; call out follow-up refactors you’d do with more time.
